correctness.rationale: PASS: Let A=H^(1/2) unbounded selfadjoint and E=dom A with graph norm. W=(I+H)^(1/2) is unitary E→Hilbert space, and spectral measure shows W(dom H)=dom A because λ²/(1+λ) and λ are comparable for λ≥1, including arbitrary kernel and spectral type. The credited von Neumann theorem gives unitary U with U dom A∩dom A={0}. Thus D=W^-1 U dom A is graph dense, D∩dom H=0. For T=A restricted to D, closure T=A and T*=A, while dom(T*T)=D∩dom(A²)={0}, yet (closure T)*closure T=H. If H is bounded, closure T is bounded everywhere and T* is bounded everywhere, so dom T*T=dom T nonzero; converse holds. Checked source proof quantifiers including H≥0 with no injectivity/compactness conditions and distinguished unclosed vs closed products. Main nonstandard theorem is the credited 1929 von Neumann separating-unitary theorem, checked in Arlinskiĭ–Zagrebnov. No computation can replace this analytic proof.
